definitions.gloss: to line up, to arrange in a row
definitions.explanation: To place things in a sequence.
To mention items one after another.

examples.japanese: {机|つくえ}を{横|よこ}に{連|つら}ねて{並|なら}べた。
examples.english: We arranged the desks side by side in a row.

examples.japanese: {理由|りゆう}を{連|つら}ねて{断|ことわ}った。
{店|みせ}の{前|まえ}に{椅子|いす}を{連|つら}ねて、{客|きゃく}を{待|ま}っていた。
examples.english: They had lined up chairs in front of the shop and were waiting for customers.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{文句|もんく}を{連|つら}ねるばかりで、{自分|じぶん}では{何|なに}もしない。
examples.english: He does nothing but string together complaints, and doesn't do anything himself.

notes:
{連|つら}ねる means to arrange things in a sequence or to list items one after another.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive)
- Pair: {連|つら}なる (intransitive, to form a line)

ASPECT (ている):
{連|つら}ねている indicates a continuing arrangement or that items remain listed.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {言葉|ことば}を{連|つら}ねる: to string words together
- {名前|なまえ}を{連|つら}ねる: to list names
- {理由|りゆう}を{連|つら}ねる: to list reasons
- {文句|もんく}を{連|つら}ねる: to complain at length

NOTE:
Often used in written or formal contexts.
